title: Commodities — Kalshi Research Exchange
description: Evidence-first paper-trading lab for Kalshi event contracts, organised around an automated forward-test desk. 28 live return-seeking strategy personas plus 2 deliberately gated ones (Form4Flash, SpreadSmith) trade open Kalshi contracts on paper from a scheduled, read-only GitHub Actions collector — a cheap tick every five minutes aimed at in-game markets and a full cycle twice an hour at :07 and :37 — and every fill, exit, settlement, intent, mark and order book is committed back to the repository. Two backtests run on verified official Kalshi price data: the original hand-collected sample (3 settled markets, 130 verified bars, 5 personas), deliberately frozen, and an archive backtest replayed bar by bar over the candle archive the collector now stores, with per-trade equity curves and a walk-forward stability split. An execution-realism check re-reads every simulated fill against Kalshi's own published trade tape via GET /markets/trades and reports the difference in cents, with a committed live result of 156 fills compared at a median absolute desk-minus-tape gap of 1.00 cent, 74.36 percent within 1 cent of a real print, 69.23 percent inside the tape's real range and 65.38 percent covered by tape volume. A season health audit (scripts/audit_season.py) checks the schedule, ledger coverage, storage compaction, signal adapters and the tape summary, re-reads settled markets against the official API on the runner, and refuses to let verify_data.py pass if anything disagrees. Simulation only: nothing submits orders to Kalshi and no API key exists anywhere in the project. IRREGULARITY: the README's own archive-backtest headline (63 markets, 2,455 verified bars, 291 trades) does not match the committed generated files at the same head, which hold 74 markets, 2,736 verified bars and 337 trade rows across 266 distinct trade ids; both sets of figures are published here and the generated files are the number of record (IRR-97).

flags: Newly added this pass: HeatConfirm, a weather rule discovered in a third-party Reddit backtest post, is traded forward precisely because its backtest claim is someone else's — the repository labels the source discovery-only and never a price source, and testing the claim forward IS the experiment.

The desk quantifies its own cron reliability rather than assuming it: IRR-34 (2026-09-21) records scripts/audit_season.py counting every scheduled :07/:37 UTC slot against committed cycles, and the committed audit shows 4 cycles with API errors out of 361 evidence-bound ledger events.
Persona count moved 20 -> 23 and the source registry 63 -> 70 entries between the 2026-09-20 and 2026-09-21 audits; treat all counts here as point-in-time.

A season-rollover layer landed during this audit ('Extend evidence-first desk across archive and season rollover'), adding data/seasons.json, a per-strategy JSON page set, an audit history log and browser plus smoke tests for the rollover path. It changed none of the published figures above.
